findings.reason: the same prose-vs-declared-closure mismatch already produced three wiring findings on s5/s6/s7 (all acted), and an undeclared dependency is what a dispatch order reads.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` has no `s9` entry, while §9's change is defined as an extension of §5's board and consumes §2's coordinator resolution, so a node dispatched on s9 would be dispatched without either dependency in its closure

findings.reason: §5's directory already owns the coordinator list, and the context-use figure is a separate capability that can ship or fail independently, so one gate proves neither.
findings.text: §9 carries two deliverables, the host-only coordinator listing and the transcript-sourced context-use figure, and its done-when asserts each, so the node cannot be closed on one verdict

findings.reason: the record §9 names as its source cannot name the session it needs for the very case §9 was written to fix, so the node would be built on a source that is empty exactly when it matters; the plan needs a source that survives settle (the host's owner pair plus the fleet's own session→project mapping, or a census that keeps a settled child) before it is dispatched.
findings.text: §9's mechanism is a claim the census does not support: the record's `children` lists only children with a pid (`if child.pid is not None`, session_host.py:340), a settle-aware host nulls a settled child's pid (session_host.py:477-480), and a follower settles once its session has no live work (`_population_has_live_work`, crew_follow_commands.py:464-492; settle at :1532-1542), so an idle coordinator's follower has settled and its census names no session or project — and the census carries only `updated_at`, not a last-dispatch time

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/session_host.py` exists and owns `session-hosts/` (`_state_dir`, session_host.py:117-123); §9's `§5` resolves to an existing section; the plans cited elsewhere resolve with extensionless hrefs treated as `<path>.html` (a-project-reads-as-one-picture.html, the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked.html, the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches.html all exist, and the named §2/§3/§4/§7 sections exist in them).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §9's done-when names a fixture crew home, a stopped-host case, a transcript-present and transcript-absent case, and a declared negative control ("a board built from live pointers alone must fail the two-session case"); §9's prose also names the fixture and the unmeasured branch, so the measures can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §9 names no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path; its fixtures are described as fixture crew homes and the other sections' evidence lands in the plan's own evidence record (§8).
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; `power-convertor-fe` is a live session name, not a plan label, and the section cites mechanism rather than tracker prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9 rests on "Each record names its sessions and their projects", but the session-host census omits every child whose pid is null (session_host.py:333-341), and a settle-aware host sets a settled child's pid to null (session_host.py:477-480), so a coordinator with nothing in flight has a live host whose record names no session and no project — exactly the case §9 exists to surface.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §9 carries two deliverables: (a) surfacing a coordinator with no run in flight from session-host records, and (b) attaching the session's context use from its harness transcript, and its done-when asserts both.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `plan-section-depends-on` (a-coordinator-sees-the-board.html:23) declares no `s9` key, yet §9's change is "The board's coordinator list (§5) also reads …" and its row carries §2's coordinator identity, so s9's declared closure omits both §5 and §2.
